propositions: The autouse repo-isolation guard's head() probe times out at the fixed 5-second watchdog during full-suite runs despite passing sequentially, producing false teardown failures in unrelated tests.
Sequential probes measure p50 9.6ms, p90 13.1ms, p99 67ms with max 507ms; under 18-process concurrency p99 reaches 2.08s and max 3.30s, below the 5-second timeout.
Under severe host oversubscription (1-min load p50 76.4, p99 138.2 on 18-core machine), real successful probes correlate with saturated intervals but do not exceed 5 seconds even at p99.
Runtime evidence isolates post-Popen scheduling/filesystem starvation as the mechanism; PATH/Git environment contamination and test-local state are ruled out by probe identity consistency.

The 5-second watchdog contract is intentionally fixed to bound blocked children and fail explicitly; no successful probe exceeded 5 seconds in instrumented runs, so the failure is environment-or-config, not a product defect.

Operational mitigation requires avoiding overlapping full suites or capping aggregate pytest concurrency on the shared overloaded host; watchdog contract changes would require explicit design decision separate from this evidence.
